newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia issues list of companies to be privatised.
newsitem.headline: Croatia issues list of companies to be privatised.

text.p: Croatia published on Friday a list of assets which will be offered in exchange for vouchers under a mass privatisation scheme to be launched soon.

"Drawing up the list and its publishing is only one in a series of steps that we have to undertake in such an important project as voucher privatisation," Privatisation Minister Milan Kovac told a news conference.
The list includes three groups of companies with a total nominal value of around 18 billion kuna or five million German marks, he said.

This amount was designed to top an estimated maximum demand by the scheme's beneficiaries, mostly victims of the 1991-95 war with Croatia's separatist Serbs and their families,said the assistant minister Damir Ostovic.
Their exact number is as yet uncertain but a registration and a media campaign to present procedure to the general public begins in April, he said.
Each beneficiary is expected to be entitled to around 7,000 privatisation points which will be exchanged for stakes ranging from under one to 100 percent in some 800 firms.

But government officials would not venture a guess which assets would be most interesting to voucher holders. Deputy Prime Minister Borislav Skegro only advised them to hang onto the shares they get in exchange until their prices rise.

"I remember when we offered 175 million marks shares in Pliva on the Zagreb Stock Exchange (at a discount) for blocked foreign exchange and no one was interested," said Skegro, until recently president of the state privatisation agency board.
Pliva, which is said to be in a lock-up following its flotation last spring, was not included in mass privatisation.
A longest list of assets that will be offered features the country's hotels on the Adriatic coast and inland, leading food companies Podravka and Kras, textile firm Varteks and shippers.
It includes stakes in loss-making industry next to minor holdings in mostly privatised companies such as profitable grocery chains Konzum and Diona.
The government also offered 32 percent in the electrical group Koncar, which will be floated as part of plans to privatise it later this year.

Whole petrochemical plants, 27 percent of the national flag carrier Croatia Airlines, a seaside marina and two percent in Slovenian ski-maker Elan appear on a list of assets previously owned by the state-owned oil company INA Industrija Nafte.
A separate list consists of firms in the regions that are still or have been held by Serbs. These will be offered to their former employees or displaced people from these areas.
